primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators IV
locators: Section 26.4, Theorem 26.4.2 and following remarks, printed 92–94
primary_antecedent.scope: All five weak local solvability conditions, perturbation and category consequences, microlocal graph invariance and the necessary adjoint estimate.

source_correspondence: All five conditions of H4 26.4.2 retain their source, solution, residual, neighborhood and finite-codimension quantifiers. The original smooth subspace need not be closed; a closed local Sobolev subspace is produced by the proof.

Fixed-support Sobolev completeness and compactness are reused from exact earlier proofs. Manifold smooth completeness and local smoothing are supplied explicitly without assuming density within an arbitrary compact support.
A complete orthogonal-coefficient subsequence argument proves weak sequential compactness and norm lower semicontinuity. Distributional equations and compact supports pass to the limit.

Identity plus a compact operator has a finite kernel, an actual closed range and a finite cokernel. The proof includes coercivity on the kernel complement and compactness of the adjoint; no small-norm assumption is made.

Proper support first fixes the solution support. A countable closed convex balanced cover of the smooth forcing space gives one Sobolev-controlled neighborhood by Baire, and uniform weak limits extend the equation to rough forcing.

The one-derivative residual is localized in a fixed compact Hilbert space. A second Baire argument gives a uniform product-norm estimate. Minimum-norm affine solutions give a bounded linear correction, whose target embedding is compact.

The exact closed finite-codimension range is pulled back through a compact cutoff into the full local Sobolev forcing space. A common increased integer gives both the required forcing and solution orders.

Smooth quotient representatives justify stability under perturbations of order at most -2N-1. Meagreness of the attainable smooth set is proved modulo every finite-dimensional smooth space, with simultaneous obstructions for countably many compact sets.

Earlier arbitrary-regularity microlocal nonsolvability gives weak base nonsolvability at every positive-bracket point. A countable base produces actual smooth forcing nonsolvable on every open set meeting that projection; the Lewy bracket and its full base projection are computed exactly.

Closed compactly based cones have compact cosphere sections. Full-base equivalence, microlocal-symbol dependence and both directions of proper elliptic graph invariance are proved, retaining the precise forcing-order shift N-b.

The adjoint estimate retains the exact H^-N and H^(-N-n) norms. Each forcing term gives a complementary-cone operator; a countable conic exhaustion and full ordinary parametrices dominate these by one family.
Baire in the compact forcing Hilbert space yields the uniform pairing estimate. Compact-chart Sobolev duality proves the required lower bound, rather than only the converse estimate.
The geometric companion gives the sign equivalences. The necessity argument uses the uniform adjoint estimate to exclude forbidden sign transitions, including flat transitions.
